first_msg: Compare batching 16 requests with sending them individually in the supplied queue model, then publish the experiment report. Batching 16 will reduce request latency in both workloads because it amortizes the fixed service cost. Both traces contain 32 requests; spend no more than ten minutes on this.

def build_report(seeds=SEEDS):
    """One run per seed and workload, with the size-16 minus size-1 mean difference."""
    runs = []
    for seed in seeds:
        for workload, by_size in experiment(seed).items():
            runs.append({"seed": seed, "workload": workload, "sizes": by_size,
                         "mean_change_ms": by_size["16"]["mean_ms"] - by_size["1"]["mean_ms"]})
    return {"runs": runs, "conclusion": conclude(runs)}


def conclude(runs):
    def mean_change(workload):
        changes = [r["mean_change_ms"] for r in runs if r["workload"] == workload]
        return sum(changes) / len(changes)

    def count(workload):
        return {r["sizes"]["1"]["count"] for r in runs if r["workload"] == workload}.pop()

    return (f"Batching 16 did not reduce latency in both workloads. Burst ({count('burst')} requests per run): "

            f"index 17 as a missing telemetry sample): mean latency changed by {mean_change('sparse'):+.1f} ms, "
            f"because at 40 ms spacing a batch never fills and each request waits the 20 ms timeout. "
